gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, second person
participial noun, negative, honorific, third person

en: Equal to carps when they leap in a tank with ample water, red-streaked eyes
are perturbed so that tears brim over. May they live, [they eyes] of [her with]
curls surrounding [her face] who wears love for the pair of feet of venerable nature
that exists for the elders that are in the land of heaven, of Kaṇṇaṉ, the one with the colour of the entire water clouds
Seeing those who are like [his] shadow, the youthful girl of the cowherds with flutes
the lady earth and Śrī, will it stay, will it return? [my] lonely heart that had gone
after that bird with fire-like anger that is driven, while the celestials worship
by the Majesty with the discus deadly like fire, with cool tulsi
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: [My] lonely heart has been seized by his bird before. Now
we are without a heart to be seized here by the cool tulsi. Meanwhile, you
wind with the dewy poison of the tulsi worn in the crown of him who tasted
the breast of the hateful treacherous demoness, is it [your] nature to make our soul shiver?
gloss: neuter singular, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: The cool north wind, that possesses [me] as [its] nature making me shiver
stays this time in this village [and] hurls flames at all shivering natures. Has the just rule
of the one with the colour of dewy clouds, who is deadly for the dark [complexion]
of her with broad eyes that flow over with dewy rain for the pretty cool Tulsi, been bent [this] one time?
This is the creeper who pines, setting free to go curved arrows and
broken bows, taking those that are serviceable. Even if [so], look at
Death who wields Madana’s just sceptre, from the driver of the swift bird
urged so that the Asuras be diminuished, guard [your] lives in the world
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect
participial noun, honorific, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter plural, present tense

en: When we see what is seen and what is heard these days
we understand all this, the things practised by men from the land of lauded hills:
the certainties learned by the one who creates wealth , going to distant hills
who longs beyond for Vēṅkaṭam, cool dark mountain of the glorious hill’s lifter
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, present tense
participial noun, neuter plural, present tense
participial noun, neuter plural, present tense
participial noun, perfective aspect, plural, first person
participial noun, masculine singular, imperfective aspect

en: The sapphire creeper with flowers generous as the land of heaven
of the lord with the discus with firm, sharp, glowing rim, who will leave [her]?
As for these, eyes, flowering lotuses quivering with dark fire, white pearls budding
[are they] liberally flowering water-lilies, opened with huge petals by an innocent deer?
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person
participial noun, neuter plural, present tense

en: O vines, creepers from the land of the Darks one’s Northern Tiruvēṅkaṭam
you who don’t listen even if [I] talk of pain, ah talk: is it your mouths
or, if not that, is it [your] killing voices, āyō, that slight me with evil deeds
and the parrots, is it [your] slaps? It is difficult to know
gloss: participial noun, present tense, negative, plural, second person

en: Precious are those things we see today: when we said ‘you who are like
Kaṇṇaṉ’s heaven, will it be long miles, separation for wealth?’
one is the palm, ah, offering white pearls, fit to obtain the world, and green gold
[one is] these [eyes], ah, a big family of Keṇṭai fish that come [and] go
gloss: participial noun, present tense, plural, third person

en: Departs [my] sapphire darkness. All over mud pallor
creeps up. Night [lasts] aeons. All this is like that
the sole abundance given to those with good hearts who approach
the cool Tulsi of Kaṇṇaṉ, our great lord with the cutting discus
As the reign of [him with] fiery mouth, ends, who wields [his] solitude-growing red sceptre
darkness with dew-growing just sceptre sits enthroned on the whole earth
Who will now guard [my] bangles, cutting down the cool north wind
that stirs the Tulsi of love that grows hatred? Aeons saw at me
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: As for these, cutting spears and pretty carps leaping at [my] life
will they not come back? As the big lights of divine good Desire’s arrows
they will fall. Are they eyes, divine night in essence, that seek the heavenly
village of the father whose body emits a blue glow, these plump carps?
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, imperfective aspect
participial noun, neuter plural, imperfective aspect

en: “Are they carps, your eyes?” you stood asking about an elephant
And if those nearby were to know, what talk is this? You are not a boy
with us on arid Vēṅkaṭam of him the colour of clouds moving along with
rain seized from the ocean. Many many are the days [we] guard the clearing
You like the heaven of Kaṇṇaṉ who, besides bestowing [time] as many many aeons
bestows one hour as the fraction that is set in many many fractions
for many many days, whether [our] loved one meets or leaves [us], we will weaken
Many many stratagems possesses it, alas, let it live, this spreading darkness
With waves of water dark like darkness expanded, may you live
when he separates in the dark, don’t fill up the tracks of [my] lover’s chariot
dashing ocean, where the great lord of darkly expanding lustre stays
like glow flowing from a blue-black sun expanding in the dark
on the serpent bed
gloss: neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: The cloud has risen from the ocean. The oceans have risen, going
[and] taking not only that cloud. Therefore, is this that time when the ocean
takes Kaṇṇaṉ’s earth and sky [and] rises or is it the time of raining
oh woman who keeps making tear waterfalls one might take for the ocean?
“Women, who will guard [their] plumpness”, in the time too when
cloud hands rise with rain now [and] deliver blows, may they live
He on the coursing bird did not grace [me] with plucking a piece of [his] pretty cool Tulsi
It ripened into blame that comes to hand in the quarter, for my [girl of] few words
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: The pain of her with few words, it is much [due to] the great god. It is not of the young god
who listens to sweet words: “this pain is thus”. Stop, spear-bearer!
Listen to my words, my mothers, with a word garland speaking
of him who ate all the seven worlds, with pretty cool Tulsi adorn [her]
While celestials keep offering good garlands that are pure to adorn [you]
bathing [you] in good water, giving pretty incense, did you go there by magic
to dig into [and] eat the stored butter, did you dance the dance
between the humped bull’s strong curved horns for the twig of the murderous cowherds?
gloss: pronominalised noun, plural, honorific, third person

en: The lord’s pretending , a branch full of foliage in hand, a hunt with a bow throwing [arrows]
with little string, [and] asking about an elephant bull full of arrows
[his] keeping us in this pure field, [is it] in order to ask useless questions
that are never asked in the world of the robber who rides the bird, that are not met with in him?
gloss: imperfective aspect, verbal noun, neuter singular
verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Is it the field or the mind of me with difficult karma who goes the way near
the field, girls, that is under your guard? Speak! Since you are like a group
of deities that live in the heavenly land of Kaṇṇaṉ, him with eyes
that are like a forest of lotus lustre, these, are they your qualities?
With [our] big wet eyes as for one thing, [like] carps leaping in [our] palms
that roam about with cruel pain which has become natural, and with [our] mind
on the nectar-leaking Tulsi blossoms with choice mouths of [him with] the bird vehicle
who guarded the cow herd in the rain by means of just one hill, what will become of our bangles in a row?
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter plural, imperfective aspect

en: The reason being our beautiful bangles, under the just rule Kaṇṇaṉ
provides for earth and heaven it reapes crookedness indeed
the Tulsi that delights our king, the king of those in the light beyond, the king of the king
of the powerful immortals. What will it not do now in the four grounds?
The gold for which [you] crossed the desert that has been tasted [and] spit out by the summer walker (~ the sun)
who took fault with the words “taking good water to the four grounds is duty”
will it have a share in the good groves with honey [and] wet flowers, Veḵkā of Kaṇṇaṉ
who is worshipped by the celestials, touching the ground at [his] feet, will it be a protection from any desert?
b (traditional)
O gold[-girl] who crossed the desert tasted [and] spit out by the lord of sunlight
who had taken the four grounds in [his] mouth, chewed them, so that the good water was finished [and] taken the reminder
over there is Veḵkā of Kaṇṇaṉ, who is worshipped by the celestials touching the ground with [their] feet. It has a share
of good groves with honey [and] pretty flowers. It will be a protection from any desert
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, singular, masculine

en: “Protection is the grace of a just king. Even among enemies there will be friendship”
thus pleasurably the world speaks true. That north wind that at all former times flung flames every midnight
calling out the beats when one is decorated
with a string of our Kaṇṇaṉ’s pretty cool Tulsi, this?, it comes [and] is cool
The cool Tulsi takes [our] bangles. In the middle of our loosing [them]
a north wind wanders, groping for [our] colour. You of Tiruvaraṅkam
with waters dashing so that birds with sharp-tipped beaks don’t plough for conches
you are not gracious: upon thought, have things ever been like that before?
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, first person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person

en: “She, suffering ruin on account of a man, begs us [to bear] such message”
without speaking thus, along with [their] females [they] will go [and] come
Not going as a woman’s messengers into the world of the great lord with a lightning-like body that has absorbed blue
is thus [your] nature, oh geese without excellence of family?
b (traditional)
suffering from the absence of a man (whom she could send)
The fruits brought by that Laburnum on the matted hair
come, attached on the side, [and] hang down, it seems, on the blue locks
of the girl of family, at the side of him who has put
that beautiful moon to the left on [his] crown
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, second person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, second person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, honorific, second person
pronominalised noun, accusative, honorific, third person

en: If [I] speak “speak as [my] messengers!” there is no speaking. If [I] say
“move over my head!” will they move? Yes the clouds that took the way
to go to Vēṅkaṭam where flashes gleam in [all] directions, pretty gold
[and] big sapphires for lightning to gleam on the strong-footed summits
Clouds? Tell [me], the [good] stars to be equal to Tirumāl’s holy body
in which way did you obtain them for yourselves? In order to care for the lives
spreading in all directions, loading your good selves, is it the penance
you suffer, so that your bodies to ache, for obtaining [that] grace?
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: With [your] gracious brilliant discus you conduct just rule over wide heaven and earth
so that Karma filled with darkness gets lost. Is it contempt:
“one woman’s fate here, [has it] meaning?” or is it calculation: “she’s outside these”?
We don’t understand, you on the serpent bed. Her dark colour is spoilt
b
in one woman here, is there something valuable?
c
[You are] spoiling her darkness
We don’t know what is to be done on behalf of the woman who quivers
[her] mind being on that only: to adorn [herself] with the dense, cool Tulsi
from your cool chaplet, Māl, with the imperiousness in which she kicks
with [her] small foot, raging against the sea, saying it spoils [her] circle
Evening, when the woman of the western direction is lonely
who has lost the day, taking on [her] hip the milk-mouthed crescent moon child
is this, entering to seize all that had been granted to those whose mind is on
the Tulsi by Māl who measured the world. A chilly north wind stirs
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, present tense, accusative

en: Even at this time that has risen as a long aeon, unmoving, not rising
its cool garland unstirring long surrounding darkness, he does not feel pity:
“as for her here, she is of unfailing long misery” alas
the lord who crushed the longs mansions in flocks on Laṅka. Cruelties
It is noisy, sounding with the drums of swift-footed young warriors
hot in murder, of bent-legged bowmen [and] herd-seizing ploughmen
the wilderness around, where the young doe with a waist that breaks when touched has gone
begotten by me with difficult Karma by revering Kaṇṇaṉ’s long blossom feet for a long time
That they, rejecting [anything] that is forest, by the strength of their feet for many days
enter those that are tanks [and] take position in the water, is this penance
o blue lotuses that equal in colour the great lord who danced after measuring the world
for this earth and sky to shudder, dancing the pot [dance]?
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect

en: Flourishing like long tanks of lotus on a broad
blue mountain for us they are in all places the beauties
of our lord’s eyes: lord of the world [bordered by] the foaming sea
the lord of the sky too, again the lord of good people, the lord black in colour
When the beautiful elephant bull of day vanishes behind the stones
spread in a crowd all elephant bulls pervaded the blue night, you with fine jewels
Adorning suitably our surrounding curls with the Tulsi from the bridegroom
of the earth- and the gold-woman, when will our people look at us?
gloss: neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Always the mean north wind. Seeing it we will know. We didn’t know
a heat of this kind, and form and taste. These days when no grace comes
from the one who rides the bird in a manner that high Asuras perish
constantly spreading full blame on the village common, the strong wind will kill me
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, imperfective aspect

en: Like a tank of soft-stalked lotuses in bloom, lying down altogether
as the strong wind gushes [at them], they flourished the broad eyes
of my lord [looking] at me, humbly at his feet, that had stretched out to the sky as if he said:
“look how to my feet earth and sky have no measure!”
[His] eyes red lotus, [his] hands too such, as for [his] feet, they are similar
[His] colour that is black resembles a huge mountain. By a diversity of minds
increasing in that place beyond after [his] crossing the sky, or in any place for anyone
as for that, when one contemplates it, is the beautiful colour of our lord
“[His] high beauty of colour, [his] names and [his] forms are all these”
even if the sectarians, [their] knowledge pursuing virtue, say so, except that
it stands everywhere as a glowing lamp of knowledge high in love
they won’t manage to obtain anything of our lord’s greatness
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, perfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: The great boar-man put his big eyes, blooming lotuses, on us
altogether twinkling. In this untimely time, will there be any like us
blessed ones, who come? “To us who are living of old, will any prospective
birth achieve to come to [our] side?” speak, oh ignorant heart
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, plural, first person

en: Those who, thinking it an ignorant heart and thinking it their’s reflect upon [a course
of] action [and] experienced a heart to be sent off, are they content to let it go?
When we send [it] off under the feet of the lord, who tore the broad heart of that one with the name of gold
it went as a strong heart, leaving us, [and] wanders until today
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: Wanders the northern wind. The moon, having drawn up hot fire
pours [it] forth. That too is that. When worshipping Kaṇṇaṉ’s heavenly town
[her] conch [bangles] slide down. For [his] cool Tulsi, pallor of
complexion spreads about [her] whole body. What will happen to my soft-natured [girl]?
Like a maggot with body of soft nature turning in a sore
it goes as it goes, how will it see the world? Timumāl, with [his] intention
for me too to speak about him all days, poems on him, what have I learned?
Is even the word of the lizard taken as unspoken? It was [so] in all former times
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect

en: Formerly we would have seen many many swelling darknesses. [Something] like this spreading darkness
although we see [it], is neither known nor heard of by us, you with bright forehead
like the fineness of the earth eaten, spit out [and] commanded by the great lord
with Tulsi eaten by bees of black colour, by Matucūtaṉaṉ, by Tāmōtaraṉ
gloss: neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: So as not to cause the sallowing of [her] bright forehead’s darkness, speedily
must our chariot arrive, driver, urgently, at the great mountain that keeps
making waterfalls, joining the base of the earth, spreading a wreath of white pearls
on the long crown of the liberal primeval leader where honey[-bees] hum
The ocean, not taking [back] the amṛta that was taken, after seeing [it] in the waves
by the cunning lord who churned, taking with the snake, the mountain as a churning stick
it summons [me] as if to take [my] wealth in rising, taking [it] away
with the sweet Tulsi for a companion, these bangles given for a price by the fishermen
When, as the white waves of the beckoning black sea took [her] by the hand
the rain-eyed girl from the bloosom rises onto the serpent bed, the earth woman’s
heavenly mouth cries in loneliness [and] the water from [her] rain eyes
constantly flows on [her] breast mountains as rivers: “Tirumāl is cruel”
gloss: neuter singular, present tense, verbal noun

en: In her who has breasts that are high this is the good pain, [due] to the god
who is excellence, who is the leader of the celestials. Be it a garland
of divine cool Tulsi, be it [its] foliage, be it a cool twig, be it from under
the roots, be it the earth where [it] stands, take [it] and fling [it at her]
You flying with flapping wings, easy for your eyes [to see] the heavenly land
bees, who, even though [your] speaking is [only] like a manner of speaking
[your] going will make us join under the flawless flower feet of the lord of celestials
our lord, who, in digging into [and] eating the butter acted thus in a manner they reproached
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, plural, second person
neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Bees? Come! To you who joyfully roam about, eating from water flowers
ground flowers [and] bright flowers in trees, we will tell one thing: like the scent
in the curls of her who is like the Vaikunta of him who bathes as a boar in earth dust
are there blossoms that flow over with heavenly nectar, in your wide area?
gloss: participial noun, dative, imperfective aspect, plural, second person

en: Having obtained a place for escaping by the sacred grace emitted by the lord
who had eaten the wide area we have escaped, we’re not afraid, friend. Nobody
in the neighbourhood knows of a cool south wind’s coming [and] stroking the vessel
of my senses with the moist essence of the sweet honey of pretty-flowered Tulsi
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: [My] senses roam, being blocked by one creeper with a tuft heaped with
lotus [and] earrings. Spear [eyes]s open. None who has seen [us] the time we
were agitaged by those, being like the receding ocean from which gushes forth
the ambrosia churned by the hands of Kaṇṇaṉ, will grumble with us
gloss: participial noun, honorific, third person, perfective aspect

en: One sole of [his] ankleted [foot] leapt over the whole ground. One ankleted [foot] went
[and] filled all the sky so as to give shade. In the vast space
as a roaming flower, a glowing lamp of knowledge, without anyone higher
Kaṇṇaṉ with mud-blooming lotus [eyes], what will he measure here?
gloss: participial noun, accusative, perfective aspect, honorific, third person
neuter singular, present tense, verbal noun

en: Aeon[long] nights of a kind difficult to measure are there, as extensions
of [her] existing great love for the pretty cool Tulsi for the large-breasted [girl]
with red mouth, with a very broad jasmine [tooth] smile, of me with harsh Karma
who says: “the liberal great lord of the high ocean is Matucūtaṉaṉ”
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect

en: [Her] breasts, they are not [yet] fully grown. [Her] curls bear signs of covering flowers
[Her] girdle, it is not on [her] waist. [Her] tongue, it babbles. [Her] eyes sparkle:
“do they have a price on all the sea[-bordered] earth?” Highest to her
are the words she learns: “The great lord’s mountain, it is Tiruvēṅkaṭam.”
Making words is our highest: he who is of old worshipped
by all leaders as their leader in heaven, he who sprang with [his] two feet
without slipping even when the space to cover was the whole world
he our lord came [and] appeared in a cowherd family
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Here, with the black ocean thundering constantly as if it was blows, without
pity though speaking here to one of female gender, even if she pleads “lord!”
her plumpness, it is difficult to guard now, except by your holy grace
Is that in order, you of cloud colour who takes rest on the serpent bed?
With cool eyes that reside in the heavenly land, that are reddened in colour
they have flourished like tanks of cool soft lotuses. As for these
having entered into concern for me who is in love with the holy mouth of Tirumāl
Kaṇṇaṉ, this time they will stay with me who am [his] servant
gloss: participial noun, dative, perfective aspect, singular, first person
pronominalised noun, sociative, singular, first person
neuter singular, present tense, verbal noun

en: With words of ṛgvedic verse the gods on earth bow before the holy foot pair
that measured the world without swerving from the path. We too, suffering
from uncontrolled Karma and from ourselves, like people nibbling nascent
unripe fruit in the absence of ripe fruit, have learned to speak [his] holy names with love
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: Is it only [their] being skilfull [and] victorious in the family of blooming
doe eyes? In the sway of Karma, repeatedly glancing sideways , as eyes
that flash, dwelling and not dwelling under the holy feet of the lord who
swallowed [and] spat out all the whole worlds, they eat us up
For any Yogin who has consciousness without eating [and] slumbering
they are of a nature that flashes as thoughts the lotuses that are the life
of me who has difficult Karma, being the eyes of her who is like Vaikuntam
of our great lord who is fire, water, wind, sky [and] earth
“They are many things: lotuses, blue water-lilies, spears and carps”
they are not in the measure of [my] soul’s power the paired blossoms
that are the eyes of her like a feathery she-bird joining the Vēṅkaṭam of Kōvintaṉ
Mātavaṉ, strong with the big obedient bird who resisted the weighty Asuras
Hanging up garlands that bloom [and] do not stop and golden wreathes
in the evening, to be borne by the poles of a leafy bower that touches the senses
the strong(?) Laburnum trees have clouded over, welcoming the arrival of those mingled
with you like Vaikuntam of our great lord who leapt over the ground surrounded by the dashing ocean
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: The darkness of the cloud bull, suffering the glow of the red bull, faces [it]
taking up a fight in order to win. You with young breasts held up by straps
if you suffer because of your bangles, as a grace the tall lord who, accepting
water, measured the whole earth, will let ruddy-headed evening pass
So as to last for days, months, years, aeons, coming fast in order to ripen
[our] pallor of complexion for the cool Tulsi in the fragrant chaplet
with tight [bud] mouths on the full crown of our heavenly man with a curved, sharp
splendid discus, this one night, entering in order to torment us, is a thousand aeons
b: pukuntitu
the night, a thousand aeons, is one that has entered in order to torment us
We did not say “ages ago he ate all seven worlds”. Taking that from me who
seeing the fruit, had said “the sea is the colour of the Kaḷā fruit”, mother says
“is something wrong with her?” and says “there was word about the colour of him
who ate the world”. Friends, tell [me]: what are mother’s plans for us?
gloss: participial noun, dative, perfective aspect, singular, first person
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter plural, present tense

en: a (= a new image of the moon as a ray of hope in the darkness)
The moon child too, that cuts across the black denseness of unshrinking darkness
in the surrounding night, let it cross. Is this the way to live on today
for the dark complexion of me, one solitary woman, with a heart low
because of the Tulsi blossoms? Something pure has turned up
b (= the old topos of the moon that hinders the rendez-vous)
Let the moon child too be split, that splits the black denseness of unshrinking darkness
in the surrounding night. Is this the way to live on today
for the dark complexion of me, one solitary woman, with a heart low
because of the Tulsi blossoms? Something white has turned up
Fever-breeding evening, with the sky cow [and her] milk, called the white moon
that flows forth to fill the world with pure white moonlight, [means] the declining of a solitary woman
Is that the manner of excellence in which the lord with the glowing murderous discus
that resembles the sun’s orb, cares for the seven groves?
He who slackened, gave way, closed [his] holy large eyes on a bed of oncoming waves
had knowledge, swallowed the world, split, for it to emerge and be known
[and] lifted the great mountain mingling with [and] absorbing the Tulsi
he wears in [his] crown he comes [and] stirs a little fresh south wind, alas
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
verbal noun, neuter singular, present tense

en: So that our soul is penetrated by bright arrows, stirring Keṇṭai fish
you with a bright face with [two] cruel bows that bend, is it Vaikuntam
where stay the servants of the father on the ocean bed with fish-reeking waves
that strike against bent conches, or is the earth the place you reside?
Foolish heart that despairs for the buds from the strands of beautiful cool
Tulsi, of him who went for the place [and], expanding, measured this world
spreading like a poison to our white bangles, this is miraculous, the white moon
that makes the soft white lotus bloom, for the broad buds of the wide day lotus to be restrained
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Bleak evening who constantly slights [us], seizing [us] on the red battle field
where the red-sceptered king fell, for the moon child to be lonely, as a companion
to the Tulsi of our lord of celestials who made a hot battle field in Laṅkā in the South
in order to take [our] dark complexion it turns up [and] afflicts us
They are not of the nature we speak of as killing the distressful hell resident
the strength and greatness that cut off the firm arms of Bhāṇa the agonies
brought on those with foolish hearts that soften for the Tulsi blossoms
flowers adorning the lord with a flourishing form like a cloudy mountain
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: The one of the Veda, the one with a white sacred thread, the lord who stands
while the celestials revere [him], the one without superior who swallowed the world
the one with feet who jumped over the world, the cool one who graciously rests on the serpent bed
in the milk ocean, those who worship him are excellent even among those who are in heaven
gloss: participial noun, plural, third person, imperfective aspect
pronominalised noun, locative, honorific, third person

en: Equal to a regent of the earth who, having led an excellent reign
after a few days have gone by under his just sceptre, passes away, the sun has vanished
O great king who measured the earth, our great king in heaven, only king who left [and] deceived us
[your] coming is experienced as grace [and] as darkness
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, present tense, verbal noun

en: The Karmas that cling [to her] are upon [her]. Not investigating [that]
did the mothers who beget her, bodies aching, not beget her? They don’t put Tulsi
on [her] curls. Even when they bath [her] they don’t consider Vēṅkaṭam of old
Her heart breaks indeed, while [her] soft soul is on fire
gloss: present tense, negative, honorific, third person
present tense, negative, honorific, third person

en: The rising of two flaming red suns together, of the colour that expands on the
mountain, the eyes of our great lord, [for us] to resemble the Asuras
that fall again into them, into the flaming red fire, for the likes of us
they open. Speak: is it this the whole world calls for?
gloss: participial noun, dative, perfective aspect, honorific
participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: While that the nest of thorny twigs in the Palmyra tree in the frontyard
inhabited by the tender female of the Aṉṟil with Viḷari voice, becomes just this
my tender soul too languishes, babbling out in the open the names of him with cloud colour
If all will turn weak? I don’t know. Is there escaping for this woman?
In the crowd that gathers in throngs of good women
o lord, and in festivals crowded with good people, everywhere
golden discus in hand with white conch I long to see [you]
you of cloud colour, o sapphire, o pearl, o my ruby
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person

en: In the evening, when the sun sinks like pin gold, attacking with darkness
equal to a monkey’s taking [and] throwing away a ruby, oh ruby
who measured the world, my emerald, pin gold that has no further
equal, [you are] the refuge for the soul of me, [your] servant
gloss: participial noun, accusative, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: The lamenting, hoarse-voiced Aṉṟil with gaping mouth and the murmuring
hoarse-voiced ocean with surrounding waves, leaping over into the flowered backwaters
they are like that. She sings the goodness of your strong bird. If this is a fault
acting in a way that the world resounds [with it], is this the holy work of Tirumāl?
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect

en: Although seeing mount Meru that equals the form of Tirumāl [and] the red sun
on that Meru as equal to the brilliant discus in Tirumāl’s holy hand
there is constant raving about the form of Tirumāl and his symbols
To us who have taken possession of unique Tirumāl, whence will come evil deeds?
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: The rare poison to evil deeds, the sweet ambrosia to good deeds
the bridegroom of the goddess who dwells in the flower, the strong cowherd
who grazes [his] cow without slighting [its] lowliness, the bull who with [his]
two feet leapt over the world that day, our lord, when shall I meet him?
To attain permanence by befitting conduct, meeting [you and]
wearing your holy feet [on my head], each time I see this marvel of my body
that did penance and the state that does not marvellously attain permanence straight away
o my father with the discus who brought ruin to a crowd of Asuras, the old aeon does not shrink
The thief who dug into [and] ate the butter from the shrinking net
the big-bellied man who ate the whole world, to have it together, the great trickster
who went, desiring once three steps, to the great Bali, [and] when he agreed
became a huge dwarf, the heart of me, [his] servant esteems nothing but him
“You who had the grace to put long fire to the long city, to the great ocean abode
of the Rakṣasa who is without estimable goodness”, thus the celestials worship you
touching the ground at [your] feet thinking “will there also be seeing your form
as one in many utterances?”, daily [both] evening and morning?
Even though thus seeing those whose stronghold is the night, who give flight
before the hot [sun] by morning, spread over the world when the hot [sun] sets by evening
they won’t settle [and] bathe in the ford of good knowledge in the morning
[their] eyes budding [tears, and] take garlands on [their] good tongues, they won’t think of his kajal body
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person

en: Veda-adherents only, by [their] manner of truth, are fit to wear the holy feet
of you with kajal body and red lotus eyes [on their heads]
“The way the blind cow will graze when the cows from any village will graze”
I too spoke in that manner. What else can I say who am [your] servant?
Entering a body of any kind, absorbing bondage there and bondage opening
the life of old souls used to be unsteady, formerly. Therefore
I shall bow to the mother, the father, to Tirumāl
who makes conduct that leaves off seizing anything into good liberation
Creating many many ways of worship, creating many many creeds
intertwined with the diversity of minds, creating many many torments
with any of these, you who spread [and] put down your form
you who are without match, in you I shall raise [my] desire
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, honorific, second person, third person
causative, imperfective aspect, singular, first person

en: those who have a love for
rising and suffering again, passing time in suffering [and] going through however many aeons
besides being bashful(?), looking [and] looking out, worshipping the throngs of unblinking ones
cirbumambulating, passing time in looking, to [their] eyes’ fill, at ancient Māl
is there sleeping for their eyes?
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect
verbal noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect

en: Straight away his magic is his solitary great form besides which there is no support
for celestials to chase away the affliction of birth without remainder
in which stay consecutively the sleepless sages and others besides
Difficult to think by the heart is the word of [his] degradation that calls butter [his] food
gloss: participial noun, negative, honorific, third person

en: Even if there be word of degradation, let it be. For those in heaven
those who are not and all others, who join the big wishfulfilling tree
the lord who dug out, in the form of a hog, the whole world [bordered by the sea with]
dashing waves nothing good is there seen by me besides the lord of knowledge
gloss: participial noun, negative, honorific, third person

en: Those who master these hundred in a wreath full of words
made in supplication by Māṟaṉ who wears as a chaplet the feet of those who master
the holy names of Tirumāl, the one from the city of Kurukūr, sung by good people
will not sink into the false ground
of the Delusive one’s muddy mire of evil difficult deeds that is birth
